name: North Dakota
summary: Statutes, constitution, administrative code and quarterly rule supplements are official PDFs on ndlegis.gov with constructible URLs (chapter PDFs t{title}c{chapter}.pdf; constit/a{NN}.pdf; acdata/pdf/{t-a-c}.pdf) read reliably by fetch_doc.py; WebFetch needs approval for built ndlegis URLs. Court rules are per-rule HTML pages on ndcourts.gov that WebFetch reads, but ndcourts.gov refuses the script (Cloudflare) and opinion and docket pages were gated for WebFetch, so Supreme Court opinion text is read from Justia (docket-keyed URLs) for now. Justia also covers the Century Code (chapter pages) and constitution; Cornell LII mirrors the Administrative Code per section. Public-domain cites 'YYYY ND N' since 1997; certiorari via supremecourt.gov dockets.

citation_map.notes: N.D.R.Ct. 11.6: opinions from 1997 are cited in public-domain form 'YYYY ND N' (no periods), pinpointed by paragraph '¶ N'; parallel N.W.2d/N.W.3d cite added when available. Temporary Court of Appeals opinions use 'YYYY ND App N'. Pre-1997 cases cite N.W./N.W.2d with '(N.D. YYYY)'; North Dakota Reports ran 1890-1953 (79 vols, per memory). Century Code numbers are title-chapter-section, each part may carry a decimal (12.1-32-01, 10-19.1-150, 4.1-01-01); the code is cited 'N.D.C.C. § …' (court style) or 'N.D. Cent. Code § …' (Bluebook). A '§§ 28-01-16 to -18' range is a span: take the first section. ND court style puts the rule set after the number ('Rule 56(c), N.D.R.Civ.P.'); both orders are covered. Routing guards: '(N.D.' also opens federal district parentheticals ('N.D. Ill.', 'N.D. Cal.'), so only the N.W. reporter form with '(N.D. YYYY)' or '(N.D. Ct. App. YYYY)' routes here; bare N.W.2d cites, bare 8-digit docket numbers and 'Administrative Rules Supplement' are context_required. CourtListener ids 'nd' and 'ndctapp' are from memory and unverified.

sources.title: North Dakota Century Code (chapter PDFs)
sources.official_status_evidence: Century Code index page (https://ndlegis.gov/general-information/north-dakota-century-code): text published on this website 'is the official version of the North Dakota Century Code'.
sources.coverage: All titles of the Century Code, one PDF per chapter; section-listing HTML per chapter.

access.pattern_rules: title and chapter = the cited numbers with '.' replaced by '-' and the integer part zero-padded to 2 digits: 28-01-16 -> t28c01.pdf; 12.1-32-01 -> t12-1c32.pdf; 10-19.1-150 -> t10c19-1.pdf; 4.1-01-01 -> t04-1c01.pdf; 4-02.1 -> t04c02-1.pdf. The PDF holds the whole chapter; the section anchor is #nameddest={section} with '.' in the title written as 'p' (28-01-16 -> 28-01-16; 4.1-01-01 -> 4p1-01-01). Fetch tools ignore the fragment, so grep the chapter text for '{section}. ' (section number + period + space). Section listings: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t{title}c{chapter}.html; title listing https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t{title}.html. www.ndlegis.gov redirects to ndlegis.gov.
access.navigation: Not needed for well-formed cites. The index page (3.6M chars) lists every section with catchline under each chapter, so it shows section ranges.

automation.robots_txt: Drupal default: Disallow /core/, /admin/, /search/, /user/* etc.; /cencode/ not disallowed
automation.notes: WebFetch on built cencode URLs and the home page ended in PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (permission prompt not answered); the index page reached via a search result worked but truncated at chapter 6-01. Large chapters exceed the fetch tool window (t10c19-1.pdf: 95 pp, 394,274 chars); use fetch_doc.py grep/section.

currency.where: Century Code index page, paragraph under the official-version notice; PDFs carry no date (HTTP last-modified only)
currency.observed: 07/01/25 UPDATE: All statutory changes approved by the 69th Legislative Assembly

hazards: whole chapter per PDF; long chapters (10-19.1) exceed the fetch tool window
decimal titles/chapters: '.' -> '-' in file name, 'p' in nameddest
statutes effective after August 1 are flagged only in the caption parenthetical
January and September 2026 special-session changes not covered by the 07/01/25 notice (check session laws)

sources.title: North Dakota Administrative Code (chapter PDFs)
sources.official_status_evidence: Index page: Legislative Council 'publishes the Administrative Code'; Internet version 'derived from the database prepared by' the Council. No official/authentication statement.
sources.coverage: All titles; one PDF per chapter; updated quarterly (initially published July 1, 1978).

access.pattern_rules: Use the first three parts of the four-part cite exactly as written, decimals kept, no extra padding: 43-02-03-01 -> 43-02-03.pdf; 75-02-02-09 -> 75-02-02.pdf; 4.5-02.1-01 -> 4.5-02.1-01.pdf; 4-07-20.1 -> 4-07-20.1.pdf. Whole title placeholder: /acdata/pdf/title{N}.pdf. Grep the chapter text for '{section}. '.
access.navigation: Index lists every title/article/chapter (chapter numbers, not section ranges).

sources.title: North Dakota Supreme Court Opinions
sources.official_status_evidence: Listing shows no official-status statement; the public-domain cite 'YYYY ND N' with ¶ numbers is the court's own citation form (N.D.R.Ct. 11.6), so pinpoints to ¶ are official-equivalent.
sources.coverage: About 12,400 entries (Oct 2026), newest first, 10 per page; page 596 of 1214 held 2002 opinions, so the listing reaches well before 1997. Each row: case name, 'YYYY ND N', docket number, filed date. Includes temporary Court of Appeals opinions ('ND App', per memory, unverified).

access.pattern_rules: Opinion pages use an internal numeric id (2026 ND 97 -> /supreme-court/opinions/210815), not derivable from the citation. Listing: /supreme-court/opinions?page={n}. Docket pages: /supreme-court/dockets/{docket} (seen as /Dockets/20220121). A GET search by citation was not tested.
access.navigation: listing ?page=N (newest first) or the 'New opinion(s)' news post for the filing date (/news/north-dakota/north-dakota-supreme-court/opinions/…) -> opinion link /supreme-court/opinions/{id}. The fetch tool's text omits the hrefs on listing pages; news posts give them.

automation.robots_txt: none (robots.txt serves the custom error page)
automation.notes: fetch_doc.py: HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge. WebFetch read listing and news pages from search results, but /supreme-court/opinions/210815, /supreme-court/opinion/2023ND32 and /supreme-court/Dockets/20220121 were PROVENANCE_REQUIRED. Opinion body text was never seen.

hazards: listing text lacks hrefs in WebFetch

sources.title: North Dakota Supreme Court dockets / Appellate Case System

access.pattern_rules: docket = 8-digit number shown on the opinion listing (Queen v. Martel -> 20220121, link seen in a news post). Search UI: https://www.ndcourts.gov/supreme-court/docket-search (case, party, calendar, document, publication search).

automation.notes: Docket page /supreme-court/Dockets/20220121 was PROVENANCE_REQUIRED; docket-search page read by WebFetch (from search result).

verification.evidence: WebFetch docket-search page: 'You do not need to register to search public appellate records'; Appellate Case System live April 8, 2024. Docket page gated.
